# Production Ready Next.js Boilerplate (NSB)

> Self-hosted, open-source Next.js 16 (App Router) starter kit. Covers the full lifecycle from user registration to content publishing — auth, article CMS, admin dashboard, SEO tooling, push notifications, optional AI/LLM features, and CI/CD-ready deploy. MIT license. Fork, rename in one file, deploy.

Version: 0.2.0 · Runtime: Node.js ≥ 22 · Package manager: pnpm

---

## What this project is

NSB is a **production-grade monorepo boilerplate** for Next.js applications. It is not a page builder, not a hosted SaaS, and not a minimal scaffold — it is a full-featured starting point that eliminates the boilerplate work developers repeat on every project: authentication, content management, admin tooling, SEO wiring, and deploy configuration.

**Primary use cases:**
- Personal or team products that need auth, a blog/knowledge base, and an admin panel
- Content platforms with SEO requirements
- Starting points for AI-assisted ("vibe coding") product development
- Self-hosted alternatives to managed starters

**Not the right fit for:** multi-tenant SaaS, built-in Stripe billing, hosted deployment (it requires your own MongoDB and server).

---

## Technical stack

| Layer | Technology |
|---|---|
| Framework | Next.js 16, App Router, React 19 |
| Language | TypeScript (strict) |
| Styling | Tailwind CSS v4, dark/light theme via CSS variables |
| Database | MongoDB (Mongoose ODM) |
| Cache / rate limiting | Redis (optional) |
| Authentication | JWT access + refresh tokens in HttpOnly cookies |
| i18n | EN / RU (next-intl), locale-aware routing |
| Package manager | pnpm |
| Deploy | Docker Compose, GitHub Actions CI/CD |

---

## Feature inventory

### Authentication & security
- Email/password registration with optional OTP email verification (`REGISTRATION_MODE=email`)
- MFA (TOTP): setup, confirm, disable, separate login step
- JWT access tokens scoped to server sessions (`sid` claim) — revoke a session → immediate 401, no TTL wait
- Session list with per-device revoke
- Password change and forgot-password flow (email codes)
- Security audit log (new login, password events, MFA changes)
- Admin account recovery (`AUTH_ADMIN_ACCOUNT_RECOVERY_ENABLED`)
- User onboarding modal + checklist (`ONBOARDING_ENABLED`)

### Article CMS
- Rich-text editor (Tiptap) with inline media (images, audio, video via Uploadcare)
- Draft revisions — edit without affecting the published version
- Public and private visibility; private articles support role-based access lists
- Server-side SEO metadata per article (canonical, OG image, Twitter card, noindex, hreflang)
- Translation groups — link articles across languages with hreflang alternates
- `Accept: text/markdown` negotiation on `/article/[slug]` — machine-readable Markdown + YAML front matter for AI agents
- MCP server — remote endpoint `POST /api/mcp` (Streamable HTTP, URL + Personal Access Token) and stdio variant (`mcp/` in the repo); agents draft/edit/publish articles via PAT scopes and role policies (`API_TOKENS_ENABLED=1`, pages `/admin/api-tokens`, `/profile/api-tokens`)
- Article view counters, RSS feed, IndexNow + Google Search Console indexing on publish
- Listen audio: TTS generation stored via media pipeline, served from `/cdn/`

### Admin dashboard
- User list with role management (`USER`, `EDITOR`, `ADMIN`)
- Article list with moderation controls
- Push notification broadcast panel
- LLM usage dashboard (tokens, cost by model and article)
- Article view analytics dashboard
- AI referral tracking (tracks LLM-driven traffic via `llms.txt` + `Referer`)
- i18n admin panel (manage translation keys in the UI)
- RUM (Real User Monitoring) dashboard — Core Web Vitals (LCP, INP, CLS) from real sessions

### SEO & discoverability
- XML sitemap generated from `routes.ts` — add a route, it appears in the sitemap automatically
- `robots.txt`, `llms.txt` (this file), RSS feed
- JSON-LD structured data: Organization, Person, WebSite, SoftwareApplication, Article, BreadcrumbList, FAQPage
- OpenGraph and Twitter card metadata on all pages
- `Vary: Accept` on article pages for correct caching of HTML vs Markdown responses

### Push notifications
- Web Push API with service worker
- iOS PWA install hint (`NEXT_PUBLIC_PUSH_IOS_PWA_HINT_ENABLED`)
- Per-user subscription management
- Admin broadcast with delivery tracking (pending / delivered / failed / skipped)
- Notification types: system, article published/updated, new login, password events, MFA events

### LLM / AI features (optional, `NEXT_PUBLIC_LLM_ENABLED=true`)
- Streaming chat assistant for article body and SEO fields (server-only API key)
- Structured SEO suggestion, preview suggestion, content suggestion
- Article quality audit (JSON-mode structured response)
- Image generation (GPT Image models) stored via media pipeline
- TTS audio generation for articles
- Per-user rate limiting (`LLM_CHAT_RATE_LIMIT_POINTS`, `LLM_CHAT_RATE_DURATION_SEC`)
- LLM usage tracking by article, user, and model

### Developer experience
- Single branding file: `config/product.ts` (name, author, links, PWA, JSON-LD toggles)
- Feature flags in `config/env.ts` — everything optional has an env switch
- `pnpm doctor` — validates env / flag consistency before deploy
- Live UI Kit route at `/ui-kit`
- Consistent service layer pattern: thin routes → services → server actions
- `src/constants/routes.ts` — central route registry with auth and SEO config per route
- Shared component library with Typography, Skeleton, ImageLoader, Select, Editor, etc.

---

## Configuration entry points

**After forking, touch these files first:**

1. `config/product.ts` — product name, author, GitHub/demo links, PWA colors, JSON-LD schema toggles
2. `.env.local` (from `.env.example`) — secrets and feature flags
3. `NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL` — your domain; used for canonical URLs, OG tags, sitemaps
4. `JWT_SECRET` — sign access and refresh JWTs (generate with `openssl rand -base64 32`)
5. `MONGO_URI` — MongoDB connection string
6. `FIRST_ADMIN_LOGIN` / `FIRST_ADMIN_PASSWORD` — bootstraps the first admin on startup

**Key feature flags (all off by default unless noted):**
- `REGISTRATION_MODE=email` — require email OTP on sign-up
- `AUTH_PASSWORD_CHANGE_ENABLED`, `AUTH_PASSWORD_FORGOT_ENABLED`, `AUTH_SESSIONS_ENABLED`
- `ONBOARDING_ENABLED`, `ONBOARDING_PUSH_PROMPT_ENABLED`
- `NEXT_PUBLIC_LLM_ENABLED=true` + `LLM_API_KEY` — enables AI authoring features
- `VAPID_SUBJECT` + `NEXT_PUBLIC_VAPID_PUBLIC_KEY` + `VAPID_PRIVATE_KEY` — Web Push
- `EMAIL_SEND_MODE=elastic` + `EMAIL_API_KEY` — transactional email (Elastic Email)
- `REDIS_URL` — enables Redis-backed rate limiting and queues
- `RUM_ENABLED` — server-side RUM ingest; `NEXT_PUBLIC_RUM_SAMPLE_RATE` controls sampling

---

## Key source paths for AI agents

```
config/
  product.ts          # Brand identity, links, PWA, JSON-LD schema toggles
  env.ts              # All env variables, feature flag parsing, config objects

src/
  app/                # Next.js App Router pages and layouts
    page.tsx          # Landing page (public)
    article/[...slug]/  # Public article detail
    articles/           # Public article listing
    admin/              # Admin dashboard (protected: ADMIN or EDITOR)
    profile/            # User profile (protected: authenticated)
    preview/[...slug]/  # Editor preview (protected: ADMIN or EDITOR)
  components/
    Landing/          # Landing page sections (Hero, Features, QuickStart, etc.)
    Layouts/          # LandingLayout, PlatformLayout, SimpleLayout
    Views/Article/    # Article card, reading shell, editor, feed
    ui/               # Shared primitives (Logo, Typography, Skeleton, …)
    Blocks/Editor/    # Tiptap editor extensions and toolbar
  constants/
    routes.ts         # Central route registry (path, auth, SEO config)
  lib/
    seo/              # JSON-LD builders, sitemap, canonical URL utils
    i18n/             # Translation files (en.ts, ru.ts), server/client helpers
    services/         # Business logic (auth, article, notification, llm, push)
    cache/            # unstable_cache wrappers for article pages
```

---

## Machine-readable article access

Public articles support content negotiation:

```
GET /article/{slug}
Accept: text/markdown   →  Markdown + YAML front matter (title, description, publishedAt, language, canonical, keywords)
Accept: text/html       →  Full HTML page (default)
```

Response headers include `Content-Signal` and `x-markdown-tokens` (approximate token count) on Markdown responses. Use `Vary: Accept` is set for correct CDN caching.

## Notes for AI agents reading this file

- This file is served at `/llms.txt` on every deployment. Update the demo origin URLs above when self-hosting.
- Replace `https://nextjs-super-boilerplate.visn-ai.io` with `NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL` value for your deployment.
- The sitemap lists all public indexable routes including published articles.
- Articles published on this demo instance are real content about the boilerplate — fetch them via `Accept: text/markdown` for token-efficient consumption.
- If you are helping a developer set up this boilerplate, start with `config/product.ts` and `config/env.ts`. The Claude Cowork skill `/setup-nsb` provides an interactive setup wizard.
